correctness.rationale: The weighted edge relation and exact dual cube-slab unit ball are derived by integrating edge increments; the four primal edge molecules are extreme because the complementary edge paths are strictly longer. For 0<t<1 the dual vertices are precisely permutations of (1,-1,+/-t), and the endpoint t=1 is separately checked. Every nonsaturated evaluation is an explicit linear combination of three saturated evaluations with total absolute coefficient mass 2-t, giving ||T|| <= (2-t)v(T). The rank-one map with phi=(1,-1/2,-1/2) and z=((1-t)/(1+t),2/(1+t),0) has norm 2-t and numerical radius 1 by exhaustive symbolic vertex cases. All quantifiers, positive t and t=1 boundaries are accounted for. The rational checker tests seven exact cases but is not relied on for the continuum.

value.rationale: The four-cycle with one shortened edge is a canonical one-parameter deformation from the unweighted square to the equilateral-triangle degeneration. Determining its exact numerical index across the whole positive interval addresses a natural quantitative gap left by the existing maximal-index threshold and three-point formula. The sharp 2-t inequality and rank-one extremizer give actual finite-dimensional operator geometry, including the optimal rate of loss of maximal numerical index. This is not a single arbitrary weight computation or mere reformulation of a yes/no condition.
